content:
Let the distance between adjacent pegs be \(1\), and use the upper-left peg as \((0,0)\).

### 1. Area of quadrilateral I
Its vertices, in order, are
\[
(0,0),\ (2,1),\ (2,3),\ (0,1).
\]
Using the shoelace formula,
\[
\begin{aligned}
[ I ]
&=\frac12\left|(0\cdot1+2\cdot3+2\cdot1+0\cdot0)
-(0\cdot2+1\cdot2+3\cdot0+1\cdot0)\right|\\
&=\frac12|8-2|=3.
\end{aligned}
\]

### 2. Area of quadrilateral II
The vertices of the solid black quadrilateral are
\[
(2,3),\ (4,2),\ (3,3),\ (3,4).
\]
Thus,
\[
\begin{aligned}
[ II ]
&=\frac12\left|(2\cdot2+4\cdot3+3\cdot4+3\cdot3)
-(3\cdot4+2\cdot3+3\cdot3+4\cdot2)\right|\\
&=\frac12|37-35|=1.
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore,
\[
[ I ]=3>1=[ II ],
\]
so the true statement is

\[
\boxed{\text{A: The area of quadrilateral I is more than the area of quadrilateral II.}}
\]
